title: Burst Pool Sizing Model v1 (Dedicated Burst Capacity)
content:
Spreadsheet-style sizing model for Redwood-managed shared burst pools (Dedicated Burst Capacity).

Purpose
- Translate Dedicated customer baselines + peak behavior into an initial burst pool size per (region, hardware class).
- Make assumptions explicit (concurrency, peak multipliers, utilization targets, supply-risk buffers).
- Provide a repeatable way to re-size pools ahead of GA and quarterly thereafter.

Status / scope notes
- v1 is intentionally simple and biased toward safety. It does not attempt cross-region balancing.
- Pool sizes here are for “managed burst pools” (shared) segmented by region + hardware class.
- Out of scope for this sheet: exact admission control algorithm, per-tenant caps, and billing rates.

========================
TAB: Assumptions (global)
========================
Units
- GPU means “1 full GPU reserved for inference runtime capacity”.
- Pool sizes are expressed in whole GPUs.
- Customer baselines are committed Dedicated GPUs.

Key assumptions (inputs)
- Expected peak multiplier (M): factor applied to baseline during bursts (e.g., 1.8x means +80% over baseline)
- Concurrency factor (CF): fraction of tenants expected to be bursting at once within a given (region, HW)
- Burst duration factor (DF): how much the bursts overlap over time (0–1). If bursts are short/spiky, DF < 1.
- Target pool utilization (U_target): planned steady-state utilization of burst pool when demand is present (kept < 1.0)
- Safety buffer (SB): extra capacity held back for supply risk + telemetry lag + incident headroom
- Coverage percentile (P): sizing to cover P% of peak windows (proxy via CF/DF)

Global defaults (v1)
- CF_default = 0.35 (assume ~35% of eligible tenants burst concurrently)
- DF_default = 0.80 (bursts overlap a lot during known peak windows)
- U_target_default = 0.70 (keep headroom for latency SLO + allocator fragmentation)
- SB_default = 0.15 (15% extra GPUs on top of computed need)
- Min pool floor = 8 GPUs per (region, HW) if we enable bursting there

Notes on “eligibility”
- Only tenants with Burst enabled and non-zero burst cap are included in the baseline pool sizing.
- For GA we should keep allowlist small; this sheet supports sizing for the initial beta/GA cohort.


====================================
TAB: Customer Baselines (input table)
====================================
Source: Dedicated contracts + fleet allocation dashboard snapshots (manual export, Jan 2025). This table is intentionally anonymized.

Columns
- Tenant: internal name
- Region: us-east | us-west | eu-west
- HW: H100 | L40S
- Baseline_GPUs: committed dedicated baseline
- Burst_Enabled: yes/no (planned)
- Peak_Multiplier_M: expected peak load factor during burst windows
- Peak_Frequency: weekly | daily | ad-hoc (qualitative)
- Notes: peak pattern / constraints

Rows (sample for model; replace with real list before GA)
Tenant | Region | HW | Baseline_GPUs | Burst_Enabled | Peak_Multiplier_M | Peak_Frequency | Notes
AURORA-SUPPORT | us-east | H100 | 24 | yes | 1.7 | seasonal | Q4 holiday + product launches
NORTHPEAK-SEARCH | us-east | H100 | 32 | yes | 2.1 | weekly | indexing jobs Sun 02:00–08:00 ET
EMBERSTACK-AI | us-west | H100 | 16 | yes | 1.6 | ad-hoc | batch eval runs; prefers short bursts
COBALT-FINANCE | us-east | H100 | 8 | yes | 1.4 | month-end | regulated; strict audit requirements
TENANT-ECHO | eu-west | L40S | 20 | yes | 1.8 | weekly | weekly ingestion
TENANT-FJORD | eu-west | L40S | 12 | no | 1.0 | n/a | not in beta
TENANT-GAMMA | us-west | H100 | 40 | yes | 1.5 | daily | diurnal peaks
TENANT-HELIOS | us-east | H100 | 64 | yes | 1.3 | ad-hoc | large baseline; low multiplier
TENANT-IRIS | eu-west | H100 | 16 | yes | 1.9 | weekly | latency sensitive
TENANT-JUNO | eu-west | H100 | 24 | yes | 1.6 | ad-hoc | burst for batch summarization

Checks
- Exclude Burst_Enabled = no from burst sizing.
- Peak_Multiplier_M should be >= 1.0.


====================================================
TAB: Region/HW Aggregation (derived intermediates)
====================================================
For each (region, HW), compute:
- Baseline_Enabled = sum(Baseline_GPUs where Burst_Enabled=yes)
- Weighted_M = baseline-weighted average of Peak_Multiplier_M for enabled tenants
- Incremental_Peak_Demand = Baseline_Enabled * (Weighted_M - 1)

Derived table (from sample rows above)

(1) us-east / H100
- Baseline_Enabled = 24 + 32 + 8 + 64 = 128
- Weighted_M = (24*1.7 + 32*2.1 + 8*1.4 + 64*1.3) / 128
            = (40.8 + 67.2 + 11.2 + 83.2) / 128
            = 202.4 / 128
            = 1.58
- Incremental_Peak_Demand = 128 * (1.58 - 1) = 74.2 GPUs

(2) us-west / H100
- Baseline_Enabled = 16 + 40 = 56
- Weighted_M = (16*1.6 + 40*1.5) / 56
            = (25.6 + 60.0) / 56
            = 1.53
- Incremental_Peak_Demand = 56 * (1.53 - 1) = 29.7 GPUs

(3) eu-west / L40S
- Baseline_Enabled = 20
- Weighted_M = 1.8
- Incremental_Peak_Demand = 20 * (1.8 - 1) = 16.0 GPUs

(4) eu-west / H100
- Baseline_Enabled = 16 + 24 = 40
- Weighted_M = (16*1.9 + 24*1.6) / 40
            = (30.4 + 38.4) / 40
            = 1.72
- Incremental_Peak_Demand = 40 * (1.72 - 1) = 28.8 GPUs

Note: Incremental_Peak_Demand represents “if everyone burst simultaneously to expected peak”. We apply CF/DF to size to realistic overlap.


============================================
TAB: Pool Size Calculation (per region/HW)
============================================
Core formula (v1)
- Overlap_Adjusted_Demand = Incremental_Peak_Demand * CF * DF
- Raw_Pool_GPUs = Overlap_Adjusted_Demand / U_target
- Pool_GPUs_With_Buffer = ceil( max(MinPoolFloor, Raw_Pool_GPUs * (1 + SB)) )

Default parameters
- CF = 0.35
- DF = 0.80
- U_target = 0.70
- SB = 0.15
- MinPoolFloor = 8

Computed pool sizes (from derived intermediates)

A) us-east / H100
- Incremental_Peak_Demand = 74.2
- Overlap_Adjusted_Demand = 74.2 * 0.35 * 0.80 = 20.8
- Raw_Pool_GPUs = 20.8 / 0.70 = 29.7
- Pool_GPUs_With_Buffer = ceil(29.7 * 1.15) = ceil(34.2) = 35

B) us-west / H100
- Incremental_Peak_Demand = 29.7
- Overlap_Adjusted_Demand = 29.7 * 0.35 * 0.80 = 8.3
- Raw_Pool_GPUs = 8.3 / 0.70 = 11.9
- Pool_GPUs_With_Buffer = ceil(11.9 * 1.15) = ceil(13.7) = 14

C) eu-west / L40S
- Incremental_Peak_Demand = 16.0
- Overlap_Adjusted_Demand = 16.0 * 0.35 * 0.80 = 4.48
- Raw_Pool_GPUs = 4.48 / 0.70 = 6.4
- Pool_GPUs_With_Buffer = ceil(max(8, 6.4 * 1.15))
                       = ceil(max(8, 7.36))
                       = 8

D) eu-west / H100
- Incremental_Peak_Demand = 28.8
- Overlap_Adjusted_Demand = 28.8 * 0.35 * 0.80 = 8.06
- Raw_Pool_GPUs = 8.06 / 0.70 = 11.5
- Pool_GPUs_With_Buffer = ceil(11.5 * 1.15) = ceil(13.2) = 14

Recommended initial pool targets (v1)
Region | HW | Pool_GPUs_Target | Notes
us-east | H100 | 35 | highest demand + highest blast radius; consider SB=0.20 given supply risk + customer mix
us-west | H100 | 14 | OK for beta; revisit if we add >2 more burst tenants
eu-west | H100 | 14 | monitor admission latency + telemetry lag; keep kill-switch tight
eu-west | L40S | 8 | floor size; L40S fragmentation risk lower but demand uncertainty higher

Operational sanity checks
- If Pool_GPUs_Target > 30% of Baseline_Enabled, re-check assumptions; may indicate CF too high or customer peak multipliers too aggressive.
- If Pool_GPUs_Target < MinPoolFloor but we still enable, floor applies to avoid “always saturated” experience.


=====================================
TAB: Sensitivity (what moves the most)
=====================================
1) CF (concurrency factor)
- us-east/H100 pool size vs CF (DF=0.8, U=0.7, SB=0.15)
CF | Pool GPUs (approx)
0.20 | ceil(((74.2*0.2*0.8)/0.7)*1.15) = ceil(19.5) = 20
0.30 | ~30
0.35 | ~35
0.45 | ~45
0.55 | ~55

2) U_target (utilization target)
- us-east/H100 pool size vs U_target (CF=0.35, DF=0.8, SB=0.15)
U_target | Pool GPUs (approx)
0.60 | ceil((20.8/0.60)*1.15) = ceil(39.9) = 40
0.70 | 35
0.80 | ceil((20.8/0.80)*1.15) = ceil(29.9) = 30

3) SB (safety buffer)
- us-east/H100 at SB 10% vs 20%
SB=0.10 => ceil(29.7*1.10)=33
SB=0.20 => ceil(29.7*1.20)=36

Takeaway: CF dominates. We should update CF using observed burst overlap once beta begins.


========================================
TAB: Notes / TODOs / Open Questions (v1)
========================================
Data improvements needed before GA
- Pull actual per-tenant peak multipliers from load-test / beta telemetry rather than sales discovery.
- Split CF by customer segment ("launch spikes" vs "batch indexing") or by time window.
- Introduce per-tenant burst caps into sizing (today we assume they can reach multiplier).

Known gaps
- Fragmentation/placement: whole-GPU model ignores allocator packing and multi-model scheduling effects.
- Admission controller behavior (queue vs fail-fast) changes how customers perceive saturation; does not change hard capacity but changes effective CF.
- Telemetry lag: if we enforce fairness using delayed usage signals, we may need additional buffer or lower U_target.

Tie-ins to guardrails
- The computed pool size is not a promise of instantaneous availability.
- Global fleet safety cap (ENG-4902) should still be able to clamp burst usage below pool size during incidents.

Suggested next iteration (v2)
- Add “Burst Eligible Baseline” per tenant: min(baseline, burst_cap_in_gpus) if we implement explicit burst caps.
- Add “Supply Risk Multiplier” by region (eu-west historically tighter supply) to inflate SB.
- Add “SLO sensitivity factor” by HW/workload to lower U_target for latency-sensitive clusters.

Owner notes (Vanessa)
- Keep this sheet as the single source for initial procurement asks for burst pools.
- Please do not paste customer names outside Redwood; keep anonymized labels in shared contexts.
